Cha Hae-in (011) at a full 4 copies adds a reliable mid-curve presence that doesn't compete with the Jinwoo slots, broadening the deck's playable card pool turn-to-turn.
weaknesses: The deck has shown zero recent tournament results and sits at roughly 2% meta share, suggesting it struggles to keep pace with faster, better-supported Tier 1 decks like REZ - Rem and CSM - Denji.

Disruption is nearly absent outside of Mutilation's effect, leaving the deck with few answers to opposing combo setups or snowballing boards from decks like That Time I Got Reincarnated As A Slime - Diablo.

Leaning so heavily on the generic Sung Jinwoo package somewhat dilutes the Han Song-yi identity, making the deck feel more like a watered-down Jinwoo deck than a distinct archetype with its own payoff engine.

Early-game tempo is below the format's aggressive decks; without an explosive turn-2/3 play, hands that stumble into Sung Jinwoo (020)/(021) without earlier support can fall behind against Kagurabachi - Iori Samura or Sakamoto Days - Shin Asakura.

The trigger suite lacks a Final trigger safety net, so once life pressure mounts against aggressive matchups, the deck has limited last-resort comeback tools compared to decks built around Final trigger density.
Resource recursion via Elixir of Life and Demon's Castle takes AP investment that competes with deploying threats, creating awkward sequencing decisions in matchups where tempo matters most.

skillRating.label: Beginner-Friendly
skillRating.reasoning: Han Song-Yi midrange requires moderate pilot skill with meaningful sequencing around resource loops (Elixir/Demon's Castle) and swing-card setup (Arise/Mutilation), but the heavy reliance on the proven Sung Jinwoo package reduces decision complexity compared to pure identity decks. Timing matters significantly for tempo swings and resource management, and matchup variance is moderate since the deck must adapt between aggressive and grindy shells. The deck is neither forgiving (limited disruption, weak early game) nor autopilot (resource loops demand sequencing), placing it solidly in the mid-skill range.
